reply.overview: [[Avatar Aang // Aang, Master of Elements]] leads a five-color Ally deck built around the four bending types, turning each bend into a card and eventually transforming into a card-drawing, life-gaining threat. With [[Aang, the Last Airbender]] or [[Aang, Swift Savior // Aang and La, Ocean's Fury]] alongside [[Appa, Steadfast Guardian]] and [[Avatar Aang // Aang, Master of Elements]], the deck assembles infinite creature ETB and LTB triggers, infinite tokens, and infinite storm count.

strategy.text: Ramp with pieces like [[Sol Ring]] and [[Arcane Signet]] to cast [[Avatar Aang // Aang, Master of Elements]] around turn 3.
Trigger all four bending types to draw cards and flip into [[Aang, Master of Elements]].
Assemble [[Aang, the Last Airbender]], [[Appa, Steadfast Guardian]], and [[Avatar Aang // Aang, Master of Elements]] for infinite creature triggers.
Use Lesson spells like [[Waterbending Lesson]] and [[Water Whip]] to refill your hand while bending.
Grow creatures and lands with earthbend effects such as [[Earthbender Ascension]] and [[Earthbending Lesson]].

keep.text: [[Appa, Steadfast Guardian]] with early mana to flash him in for value.
A hand with ramp like [[Chromatic Lantern]] fixing colors for your spells.

sendBack.text: A hand stuck in one color with no way to fix for five colors.
A hand with no early plays before turn 4 to cast your commander.

tips.text: [[Aang, the Last Airbender]] airbends a permanent so [[Appa, Steadfast Guardian]] can make an Ally token when it's cast from exile.
[[Toph, Hardheaded Teacher]] returns a Lesson from your graveyard while her earthbend trigger grows a land.
[[Uncle Iroh]] lowers Lesson costs, helping cast [[Waterbending Lesson]] more easily.

keyCards.card: Avatar Aang // Aang, Master of Elements
keyCards.job: Draws cards off bends and flips into a finisher.
Airbends a permanent, enabling the infinite loop.
Makes tokens off spells cast from exile, loop piece.

keyCards.card: Aang, Swift Savior // Aang and La, Ocean's Fury
keyCards.job: Alternate airbend piece enabling the infinite loop.
Reduces Lesson spell costs for easier casting.
Recurs instants or sorceries while growing lands.
Grows and draws cards off opponents' searches.

assessment.line: The deck only answers artifacts or enchantments through [[Origin of Metalbending]].
Only 2 interaction cards with 1 at instant speed leaves little to stop a fast combo like [[Appa, Steadfast Guardian]] looping.
Much of the card draw engine stops if [[Avatar Aang // Aang, Master of Elements]] is removed or taxed.
Removing [[Appa, Steadfast Guardian]] before the loop starts breaks the infinite combo entirely.
Five-color demands force reliance on fixing like [[Chromatic Lantern]] or risk color screw.

reply.overview: This Colorless deck ramps hard into [[Zhulodok, Void Gorger]] and other huge colorless spells, turning every mana-value 7+ cast into a double cascade that chains into more spells and board wipes. [[Basalt Monolith]] and [[Forsaken Monument]] combine for infinite colorless mana once assembled. The deck grinds opponents down with Eldrazi value creatures, mass exile effects, and artifact ramp before closing with giant threats or the infinite mana line.

strategy.text: Ramp hard early using artifact mana rocks to reach big mana fast.
Cast [[Zhulodok, Void Gorger]] around turn 5 to enable double cascade on huge spells.
Cascade off cards like [[Kozilek, the Great Distortion]] or [[All Is Dust]] to chain value and wipes.
Assemble [[Basalt Monolith]] and [[Forsaken Monument]] for infinite colorless mana.
Close games with Eldrazi beaters or by dumping mana into activated abilities like [[Steel Hellkite]].

keep.text: A hand with [[Sol Ring]] and a plan to chain into more ramp is strong.
Early mana rocks like [[Thran Dynamo]] that lead into big colorless spells are great.

sendBack.text: [[Sol Ring]] with nothing to cast after it stalls out.
A hand lacking any path to 7 mana for [[Zhulodok, Void Gorger]] struggles.

tips.text: Cast [[Kozilek, the Great Distortion]] after [[Zhulodok, Void Gorger]] is out to trigger cascade twice off one spell.
Use [[Basalt Monolith]] with [[Forsaken Monument]] on the battlefield to generate infinite colorless mana.
Untap [[Basalt Monolith]] repeatedly while [[Forsaken Monument]] doubles each tap for colorless mana.

keyCards.job: Grants double cascade to big colorless spells.
Combo piece for infinite colorless mana.
Combo piece doubling colorless mana production.
Refills hand and counters spells via discard.
Exiles colored permanents and closes games.
Strips a card and adds an Eldrazi body.
Mass exile of colored permanents board-wide.
Exiles all nonland permanents to reset board.

assessment.line: The deck leans on exile effects like [[All Is Dust]] rather than graveyard recursion, so grave hate matters little.
The deck depends on artifact mana rocks like [[Sol Ring]] and has no dedicated answer to an opposing artifact or enchantment.
With only 3 instant-speed pieces, a fast combo can resolve before [[Not of This World]] can stop it.
Without [[Zhulodok, Void Gorger]] on board, big colorless spells lose their cascade and the deck slows dramatically.
The deck wins through multiple large threats and card advantage rather than a single combat route, lessening reliance on fogs like [[Propaganda]].
Removing [[Basalt Monolith]] before [[Forsaken Monument]] joins it denies the infinite mana line.
As a Colorless deck with 38 lands and heavy land-based mana fixing like [[Urza's Tower]], color screw is not a concern.

reply.overview: [[Gishath, Sun's Avatar]] leads a Naya Dinosaur deck that ramps toward an around turn 7 cast, then swings in to cascade creatures off the top of the library. Enrage triggers on dinosaurs like [[Polyraptor]], [[Bellowing Aegisaur]], and [[Forerunner of the Empire]] can chain into repeated token creation and counters, closing games through combat and attrition rather than a single line.

strategy.text: Ramp with pieces like [[Sol Ring]] and [[Arcane Signet]] toward casting [[Gishath, Sun's Avatar]] around turn 7.
Attack with [[Gishath, Sun's Avatar]] to reveal cards and put Dinosaurs onto the battlefield for free.
Trigger Enrage on [[Polyraptor]] and [[Bellowing Aegisaur]] to flood the board with tokens and counters.
Use [[Forerunner of the Empire]] to find Dinosaurs and chain damage into more Enrage triggers.
Close the game with trampling attackers backed by [[Garruk's Uprising]] and [[Rite of Passage]] growth.

keep.text: A hand with early ramp and a path to [[Walking Ballista]] as a late payoff is fine.
Keeping lands plus a Dinosaur like [[Polyraptor]] sets up the midgame plan.

sendBack.text: A hand missing red or white sources can't cast [[Gishath, Sun's Avatar]] on curve.
Too many high-cost spells with no ramp stalls before casting [[Annoyed Altisaur]].

tips.text: [[Bellowing Aegisaur]] dealt damage puts counters on [[Polyraptor]], which then makes a copy of itself as an Enrage trigger.
[[Forerunner of the Empire]] damages creatures when a Dinosaur enters, which can trigger [[Polyraptor]]'s Enrage to copy itself.
[[Marauding Raptor]] deals 2 damage to entering creatures, which can set off [[Polyraptor]]'s Enrage repeatedly.

keyCards.job: Puts free Dinosaurs onto the battlefield on combat damage.
Copies itself whenever it takes damage, building a board.
Spreads +1/+1 counters across the team when damaged.
Finds Dinosaurs and pings creatures on Dinosaur entry.
Reduces creature costs and damages entering creatures.
Removes counters to deal damage, pairs with Enrage pieces.

keyCards.card: Growing Rites of Itlimoc // Itlimoc, Cradle of the Sun
keyCards.job: Finds a creature, then flips into extra mana.
Lets you cast creatures off the top of the library.

assessment.line: Only [[Thrashing Brontodon]] and [[Zacama, Primal Calamity]] answer an opposing [[Rest in Peace]].
With 0 instant-speed answers among 7 interaction cards, a fast combo like one built around [[Walking Ballista]] elsewhere can resolve unchecked.
Without [[Gishath, Sun's Avatar]] connecting, the deck loses its main way to cheat Dinosaurs into play.
The plan leans on combat damage, so a fog effect like [[Ghostly Prison]] from an opponent slows it badly.
Removing [[Polyraptor]] before its Enrage triggers stops the token chain with [[Forerunner of the Empire]].

reply.overview: This mono Red Goblins deck led by [[Krenko, Mob Boss]] floods the board with token Goblins and turns them sideways or sacrifices them for damage. The combo of [[Goblin Warchief]] plus [[Krenko, Mob Boss]] plus [[Skirk Prospector]] produces infinite hasty Goblin tokens and infinite commander casts, and [[Goblin Chieftain]] can replace [[Goblin Warchief]] in that same loop. Outside the combo, the deck just goes wide and swings or burns opponents out with Goblin-count payoffs like [[Goblin War Strike]].

strategy.text: Ramp early with cards like [[Sol Ring]] and [[Skirk Prospector]] to get [[Krenko, Mob Boss]] out around turn 4.
Tap [[Krenko, Mob Boss]] to flood the board with 1/1 red Goblin tokens equal to your Goblin count.
Assemble [[Goblin Warchief]], [[Krenko, Mob Boss]], and [[Skirk Prospector]] for infinite hasty Goblin tokens and infinite commander casts.
Or swap in [[Goblin Chieftain]] with [[Krenko, Mob Boss]] and [[Skirk Prospector]] for the same infinite loop.
Close games with wide attacks or burn payoffs like [[Goblin War Strike]] and [[Goblin Grenade]] off your Goblin horde.

keep.text: A hand with early ramp and a piece like [[Skirk Prospector]] sets up the loop.
Keeping [[Goblin Matron]] to find missing combo pieces is a fine plan.

sendBack.text: A hand with no early plays and no red sources to cast [[Krenko, Mob Boss]] struggles.
Too many high cost spells and no way to reach turn 4 for [[Krenko, Mob Boss]] is risky.

tips.text: Sacrifice extra Goblins to [[Skirk Prospector]] for mana while [[Goblin Warchief]] keeps new Goblins hasty.
Use [[Goblin Bombardment]] to turn spare tokens from [[Krenko, Mob Boss]] into direct damage.
Feed [[Tar Pitcher]] sacrificed Goblins for repeatable damage once your board is wide.

keyCards.job: Taps to create an army of Goblin tokens.
Gives Goblins haste, combo piece with Krenko.
Sacrifices Goblins for mana, fuels infinite loop.
Alternate combo piece granting Goblins haste.
Finds missing Goblin combo pieces.
Turns dying Goblins into reach damage.
Converts spare tokens into direct damage.

assessment.line: The deck leans on enchantments like [[Goblin Bombardment]] and has no answer if opponents target it.
Removing [[Krenko, Mob Boss]] repeatedly stalls the token engine the whole plan relies on.
The deck wins mostly through wide combat, and a fog like [[Goblin War Strike]] turned back hurts without backup.
Removing [[Skirk Prospector]] at the key moment breaks the infinite loop with [[Krenko, Mob Boss]] and [[Goblin Warchief]].

reply.overview: This Jeskai God tribal deck led by [[Kratos, Stoic Father]] and [[Atreus, Impulsive Son]] grinds experience counters from attacking Gods and God deaths, then dumps huge +1/+1 counters each end step before turning them into cards and damage through [[Atreus, Impulsive Son]]'s ability.

strategy.text: Ramp early with signets and talismans to set up [[Kratos, Stoic Father]] around turn 4.
Attack with Gods like [[Purphoros, God of the Forge]] and [[Surtr, Fiery Jötun]] to generate experience counters.
Funnel the counters onto a big threat each end step via [[Kratos, Stoic Father]]'s trigger.
Use [[Atreus, Impulsive Son]] to convert stored experience into cards and direct damage.
Proliferate engines like [[Inexorable Tide]] push counters further and faster.

keep.text: A hand with [[Jeska's Will]] and early ramp into Gods is worth keeping.
A hand with [[The Locust God]] as a draw engine backup is solid.

sendBack.text: A hand missing red or white sources struggles to cast [[Surtr, Fiery Jötun]].
A hand with no early plays before turn 3 falls behind on tempo.

tips.text: [[Flux Channeler]] proliferates off noncreature spells, stacking counters faster for [[The Ozolith]] to store.
[[Tekuthal, Inquiry Dominus]] doubles proliferate triggers from [[Inexorable Tide]] for extra counters each spell.
[[Ojer Pakpatiq, Deepest Epoch // Temple of Cyclical Time]] gives rebound to instants cast alongside [[Mystical Tutor]] finds.

keyCards.job: Generates experience counters and distributes +1/+1 counters.
Converts experience counters into cards and damage.
Deals damage whenever a creature enters, fuels the attack plan.
Deals damage on historic spells, a God for experience.
Turns card draw into flying haste tokens as a backup engine.
Proliferates every spell cast, spreading counters widely.

keyCards.card: Ojer Pakpatiq, Deepest Epoch // Temple of Cyclical Time
keyCards.job: Gives rebound to instants, another God for experience.

assessment.line: The deck has few ways to remove an opposing enchantment like [[Ghostly Prison]] locking down attacks.
Losing [[Kratos, Stoic Father]] repeatedly strips the deck of its main counter engine and slows [[Atreus, Impulsive Son]]'s payoff.
Three-color demands strain the mana base when drawing a hand heavy on [[Battlefield Forge]] and other painlands.

reply.overview: This Wizard-tribal Blue deck led by [[Baral, Chief of Compliance]] casts around turn 2 and reduces instant and sorcery costs while rewarding countered spells with card draw and discard. It wins by assembling [[Naru Meha, Master Wizard]] with [[Sublime Epiphany]] or with [[Ghostly Flicker]] to create loops of infinite ETB and death triggers, or grinds opponents down with mills and counters alongside [[Jace, Wielder of Mysteries]] or [[Laboratory Maniac]] as alternate win paths through an empty library.

strategy.text: Cast [[Baral, Chief of Compliance]] early to cheapen instants and sorceries and draw off counters.
Deploy Wizards like [[Archmage of Runes]] and [[Azami, Lady of Scrolls]] to chain spells and refill your hand.
Hold up counterspells such as [[Mana Leak]] and [[Counterspell]] to protect your board and stall opponents.
Assemble [[Naru Meha, Master Wizard]] with [[Sublime Epiphany]] to generate infinite triggers once enough mana is available.
Alternatively loop [[Ghostly Flicker]] with [[Naru Meha, Master Wizard]] once seven mana is online for infinite ETB value.

keep.text: [[Baral, Chief of Compliance]] on curve with a counterspell like [[Memory Lapse]] backing it up.
Early plays into [[Naru Meha, Master Wizard]] with a way to draw more cards.

sendBack.text: A hand lacking a path to [[Baral, Chief of Compliance]]'s discount with no cheap spells to play.
A hand heavy on noncreature spells but no [[Sol Ring]] or other way to ramp into turn 2 plays.

tips.text: Copy [[Ghostly Flicker]] with [[Naru Meha, Master Wizard]]'s enters trigger to flicker extra permanents for value.
[[Sublime Epiphany]] can target itself when copied by [[Naru Meha, Master Wizard]] to counter and bounce simultaneously.
[[Archmage of Runes]] and [[Jace's Sanctum]] both cheapen the same instants and sorceries, stacking discounts.

keyCards.job: Cheapens spells and draws cards off counters.
Copies a spell on entry to enable the loop.
Counters and returns itself to loop with Naru Meha.
Flickers Naru Meha repeatedly for infinite triggers.
Cheapens spells and draws a card on each cast.
Mills and draws, offering a library-out win path.
Turns an empty library draw into a win.

assessment.line: The deck has no way to deal with an opposing artifact like a resolved [[Collector Ouphe]].
Without [[Baral, Chief of Compliance]] the deck loses its cost reduction and card draw engine on counters.
The deck has little pillowfort to stop combat decks, leaning on counters instead of fogs like [[Ghostly Prison]].
Removing [[Naru Meha, Master Wizard]] before it resolves its enters trigger breaks both combo lines.

reply.overview: [[Yuriko, the Tiger's Shadow]] leads a Dimir ninjutsu deck full of unblockable evasive attackers that slip past blockers, swap in ninjas cheaply via ninjutsu, and deal combat damage that triggers card advantage and life loss off the top of the library. The deck wins by chaining unblockable creatures into [[Yuriko, the Tiger's Shadow]] and other ninjas like [[Ink-Eyes, Servant of Oni]] and [[Fallen Shinobi]], draining opponents through repeated reveal triggers while backing the plan with counterspells and targeted removal.

strategy.text: Deploy cheap unblockable creatures such as [[Slither Blade]] or [[Tormented Soul]] early to set up ninjutsu swaps.
Bounce an unblocked attacker to put [[Yuriko, the Tiger's Shadow]] into combat from the command zone around turn 3.
Chain combat damage triggers from [[Yuriko, the Tiger's Shadow]] and [[Ingenious Infiltrator]] to draw cards and drain life.
Swap in bigger ninjas like [[Ink-Eyes, Servant of Oni]] or [[Fallen Shinobi]] for reanimation or card advantage.
Hold up counterspells such as [[Counterspell]] and [[Swan Song]] to protect the attack plan.

keep.text: An early unblockable creature alongside [[Satoru Umezawa]] to enable cheap ninjutsu swaps.
A hand with [[Ninja of the Deep Hours]] and two or three lands to curve into ninjutsu.

sendBack.text: A hand with no blue source and heavy black spells struggles to cast [[Yuriko, the Tiger's Shadow]].
A hand lacking any cheap evasive creature to trigger ninjutsu value stalls the plan.

tips.text: Bounce [[Mist-Cloaked Herald]] to ninjutsu in [[Yuriko, the Tiger's Shadow]] from the command zone for a cheap swap.
Use [[Satoru Umezawa]] to look at three cards whenever you activate any ninjutsu ability that turn.
[[Ink-Eyes, Servant of Oni]] connecting lets you reanimate a creature straight from an opponent's graveyard.
[[Fallen Shinobi]] damage lets you cast cards exiled from the hit player's library without paying mana.

keyCards.job: Drains life and draws off combat damage triggers.
Grants cheap ninjutsu to every creature in hand.
Steals a creature from an opponent's graveyard on hit.
Lets you cast cards exiled from the struck player's library.
Draws a card whenever any ninja connects.
Finds any ninja card after dealing combat damage.
Copies itself each time it connects, flooding attackers.
Generates Treasure tokens whenever ninjas connect.

assessment.line: [[Ink-Eyes, Servant of Oni]] and [[Reanimate]] both rely on graveyards; [[Bojuka Bog]] or similar hate shuts them down.
The decklist has no answer to an opposing artifact or enchantment beyond [[Commandeer]] and [[Swan Song]] catching it on the stack.
Thirteen of seventeen interaction pieces are instant speed, letting the deck respond before a fast combo resolves.
Without [[Yuriko, the Tiger's Shadow]] connecting, the deck loses its main card advantage and drain engine entirely.
The plan depends almost entirely on unblocked combat damage; a fog like [[Ghostly Prison]] would stop the deck cold, but it has none.
No assembled combo is listed in the deck, so there is no single combo piece to protect or lose.
With 27 lands heavily supporting both Dimir colors through duals like [[Watery Grave]] and [[Darkslick Shores]], color access is stable.

reply.overview: [[Kilo, Apogee Mind]] leads a Jeskai artifacts deck that proliferates counters constantly, assembling several infinite combos like [[Basalt Monolith]] with [[Zirda, the Dawnwaker]] for infinite colorless mana or [[Inspirit, Flagship Vessel]] with [[Kilo, Apogee Mind]] and [[Magistrate's Scepter]] for infinite turns, while cheap artifacts and proliferate effects like [[Tezzeret's Gambit]] keep the board growing toward those lines.

strategy.text: Cast [[Kilo, Apogee Mind]] around turn 3 and attack or tap it to start proliferating counters.
Ramp with artifacts like [[Sol Ring]] and [[Arcane Signet]] to accelerate into combo pieces.
Assemble [[Basalt Monolith]] and [[Zirda, the Dawnwaker]] for infinite colorless mana.
Chain [[Pemmin's Aura]] onto [[Unctus, Grand Metatect]] to loot and draw infinitely.
Close games with [[Inspirit, Flagship Vessel]], [[Kilo, Apogee Mind]], and [[Magistrate's Scepter]] for infinite turns.

keep.text: A hand with [[Sol Ring]] and a path into [[Kilo, Apogee Mind]] on turn 3 is strong.
Early mana rocks alongside [[Pemmin's Aura]] as a later engine piece are worth keeping.

sendBack.text: A hand with no red source struggles to cast [[Zirda, the Dawnwaker]] on time.
Too many lands with no way to reach [[Unctus, Grand Metatect]] stalls the plan.

tips.text: Enchant [[Unctus, Grand Metatect]] with [[Pemmin's Aura]] to repeatedly untap it and trigger its loot ability infinitely.
Use [[Zirda, the Dawnwaker]] to cheapen [[Basalt Monolith]]'s untap cost, enabling the infinite mana loop.
[[Kilo, Apogee Mind]] proliferates charge counters on [[Magistrate's Scepter]] faster when combined with [[Inspirit, Flagship Vessel]]'s station triggers.

keyCards.job: Proliferates on tap, enabling the deck's counter payoffs.
Untaps creatures repeatedly to power infinite loops.
Loots when tapped, the target of the infinite draw loop.
Produces colorless mana, looped infinitely with Zirda.
Cheapens activation costs to enable the mana loop.
Stations counters onto artifacts, feeds the turns combo.
Converts charge counters into extra turns.
Adds mana and enables the proliferate combo with Kilo.

assessment.line: The deck leans entirely on artifacts, so something like [[Vandalblast]] could wipe the board.
Only 6 interaction cards, 4 at instant speed, leaves little room to stop a fast combo like [[Basalt Monolith]] lines.
Removing [[Unctus, Grand Metatect]] before it is enchanted by [[Pemmin's Aura]] stops that infinite draw loop.
